create.name: Elizabeth Lesser
create.bio:
Elizabeth Lesser is an author and one of the founders, in 1977, of Omega Institute, the retreat and conference centre in Rhinebeck, New York. Before Omega she worked as a midwife and birth educator. Over the decades she helped shape Omega's programmes in meditation, yoga, spirituality, the arts and social change, and she later helped found its centre for women's leadership, an offshoot of Omega's Women & Power gatherings.

Her writing turns on how ordinary people grow through hard times and how spiritual life can be lived without dogma. The Seeker's Guide draws on what she learned from the many teachers and traditions that passed through Omega. Broken Open, her best-known book, looks at how loss, illness, divorce and other upheavals can become openings to a fuller life. Marrow is a memoir about her relationship with her younger sister, and Cassandra Speaks asks what changes when women tell the stories a culture lives by. She speaks widely, has appeared on Oprah Winfrey's SuperSoul Sunday and TED, and leads occasional retreats; her talks are warm, frank and full of stories.

books.title: Broken Open: How Difficult Times Can Help Us Grow
books.author: Elizabeth Lesser
books.description: Her best-known book, drawing on her own life and others' to show how loss and upheaval can lead to a deeper and more honest way of living.

books.title: The Seeker's Guide
books.author: Elizabeth Lesser
books.description: Her first book, a guide to building a personal spiritual life, distilled from her years among the teachers and traditions that came through Omega.

books.title: Cassandra Speaks: When Women Are the Storytellers, the Human Story Changes
books.author: Elizabeth Lesser
books.description: A look at the old myths and origin stories that still shape how we live, and an invitation for women to trust their own voices and tell new ones.

books.title: Marrow: Love, Loss, and What Matters Most
books.author: Elizabeth Lesser
books.description: A memoir of her bond with her younger sister, Maggie, and of what the two of them learned about love and honesty during a hard time in their lives.
